hero.headline: Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, cites progress in talks
hero.body:
President Trump canceled planned military strikes against Iran on Thursday, saying discussions with Iranian leadership had reached the highest levels and shown progress. Trump announced the decision in a statement, writing that he had canceled "the forthcoming strikes and bombings" based on developments in talks with Tehran.

The cancellation came hours after Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" following a second night of military exchanges between the two countries. The U.S. military had launched 49 Tomahawk missiles at Iranian targets the previous night. Trump claimed in his announcement that Iran's leadership had "approved" a draft agreement, though Tehran has not confirmed this claim.

Three sources briefed on the negotiations told one news outlet that key gaps in the talks were narrowed during meetings between Iranian officials and Qatari mediators on Wednesday. The discussions reportedly focus on extending a ceasefire, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and beginning 60 days of negotiations on Iran's nuclear program. Qatar has been serving as a mediator between Washington and Tehran.

Trump has previously claimed that a deal with Iran was near, only for negotiations to stall or break down. Iran's top negotiator issued a warning Thursday, saying that "wrong strategies and impulsive decisions will reset the entire board for the worse, explode energy infrastructure and markets and create an endless quagmire." The statement came after Trump had threatened to seize Kharg Island, a central hub for Iran's oil exports.

The situation follows escalating tensions between the two nations, with military strikes exchanged over consecutive nights before the sudden diplomatic shift. The potential agreement under discussion would mark a significant de-escalation if finalized, though details remain subject to confirmation from both governments.

cards.headline: House rejects extension of expiring surveillance law
cards.body:
The House of Representatives voted against extending a powerful surveillance law set to expire Friday, rejecting a short-term renewal measure in a 198-218 vote. The failed extension ensures that Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act will lapse, marking a significant development in ongoing debates about government surveillance powers.

The rejection came after Democrats announced they would block renewal of the law in protest of Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Pulte, a major Republican donor and head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has faced criticism for lacking relevant national security experience. House Democratic leaders including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries stated that Pulte's appointment violated legal requirements for the position and expressed concern about potential misuse of government databases.

Section 702 of FISA, enacted following the September 11 attacks, permits U.S. intelligence agencies to intercept foreign communications without court warrants. Republican leaders had attempted to extend the law for three years and sought bipartisan support for the measure. However, Democrats withdrew from those negotiations after Pulte's nomination was announced.

The extension attempt used a fast-track process requiring a two-thirds majority to pass. Republicans fell significantly short of success, with 19 members of their own party joining most Democrats in opposition. Some Republican opponents cited civil liberties concerns about the law's scope and impact on privacy rights. A Senate vote on extending FISA for three years similarly failed last week, with Democrats except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania voting against the measure.

Despite the law's expiration, surveillance operations will not immediately cease. The FISA court previously issued a year-long certification authorizing Section 702 collection through approximately March 2027. The statute contains a provision allowing collection to continue under that court order even after the law lapses. This means intelligence agencies can maintain certain surveillance activities during any gap in statutory authorization.

The development reflects broader tension between national security priorities and civil liberties protections. Lawmakers on both sides have expressed concerns about balancing government surveillance needs with individual privacy rights. Republican chairs of the Senate intelligence and judiciary committees sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio asking the administration to prepare for a potential significant gap in foreign intelligence collection.

The lapse will require intelligence agencies to adjust their operations and potentially rely on alternative legal frameworks for activities previously conducted under Section 702. The House rejection sets up potential negotiations for a longer-term solution, though the immediate expiration appears unavoidable given the current timeline and voting patterns in Congress.

cards.headline: US Producer Prices Post Largest Annual Jump Since 2022
cards.body:
Wholesale prices in the United States experienced a sharp surge in May, representing the biggest annual increase since 2022 as energy costs drove inflation higher. The spike signals growing pressure on both businesses and consumers during a period of economic uncertainty.

The producer price index measures what businesses pay for goods and services before those items reach retail customers. When producer prices rise, companies typically pass these costs along to consumers through higher retail prices. Energy played a significant role in May's increase, reflecting broader market tensions linked to geopolitical developments in the Middle East.

The May jump marks a notable shift following months of slower price growth. The data arrives as policymakers and economists closely examine inflation trends, balancing concerns about economic stability against the need to support continued growth. Producer price inflation had moderated substantially throughout 2023 and 2024, but recent months have shown renewed upward pressure.

The increase follows President Trump's recent comments on inflation. After consumer price data showed a three-year high earlier this week, Trump stated he welcomed inflation. Economists and analysts criticized this position, pointing out the burden higher prices place on households. The president's remarks came during rising tensions with Iran that have contributed to volatility in energy markets.

Energy prices have climbed significantly in recent weeks as Middle East stability concerns affected global oil supplies. While Trump reversed threats to strike Iran, the period of heightened conflict pushed oil prices higher. The national average gas price stood at about $4.16 per gallon, roughly a dollar more expensive than the same time last year, according to AAA data.

Wholesale price increases extend beyond energy to multiple sectors, suggesting inflationary pressure may persist even if energy costs stabilize. The broadening nature of these increases indicates that consumers may continue facing affordability challenges across various categories.

Consumer frustration over rising prices has grown substantially. According to the National Consumer Rage survey, nearly 80 percent of Americans experienced a service or product problem in 2025, with about two-thirds feeling angry about it. Many consumers report constantly dealing with overcharges, customer service difficulties, faulty products, and billing errors that appear to benefit companies rather than households.

The Bank of England recently warned that interest rates may need to rise if energy costs remain elevated for an extended period. The Federal Reserve and other economic authorities now face renewed challenges in managing price stability while supporting economic expansion. The current inflationary environment comes at a time when consumer confidence has weakened noticeably, with surveys showing people feel anxious about the economic outlook and potential future cost of living shocks.

cards.headline: Israel Moves to Rapidly Expand West Bank Settlements Before Elections
cards.teaser: The Israeli government is rushing to install temporary housing at approximately 60 empty sites in the West Bank before national elections this fall.
cards.body:
Israel is accelerating settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, with the government planning to place temporary housing at approximately 60 empty sites. The push to complete this expansion before national elections in the fall represents a significant increase in settlement activity.

International law considers Israeli settlements in the West Bank illegal, though Israel contests this position. Human rights groups have accused the Israeli government of deliberately attempting to annex Palestinian territory through these settlement policies.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drone Campaign Targets Russian Supply Lines to Crimea
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces struck Russian convoys and bridges in a sustained drone campaign aimed at cutting off supply routes between Russia and occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces are conducting an expanded drone campaign aimed at severing supply routes connecting Crimea to Russia. In one strike, drones hit a Russian convoy of approximately 50 fuel and ammunition trucks near Armiansk in Crimea. Ukraine's drone commander stated the objective is to isolate Crimea by disrupting Russian logistics operations.

The campaign has also targeted bridges in occupied Kherson that serve as critical supply routes for Russian forces. By attacking infrastructure supporting troop movements and deliveries, Ukrainian forces aim to undermine Russian military operations in the region.

cards.headline: Trump nominates Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: The president selected the former SEC chairman and current Manhattan prosecutor for the top intelligence post.
cards.body:
President Trump announced his nomination of Jay Clayton as director of national intelligence. Clayton previously served as chair of the Securities and Exchange Commission and currently holds the position of U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.

The nomination came after Trump faced widespread criticism for initially installing controversial ally Bill Pulte as acting director of National Intelligence. As director of national intelligence, Clayton would oversee the nation's intelligence community and serve as the principal intelligence advisor to the president. The position requires Senate confirmation.

cards.headline: Pakistan Airstrikes Kill 13 Afghan Civilians, U.N. Confirms
cards.teaser: Pakistani airstrikes on the border killed 13 Afghan civilians, mostly women and children, according to U.N. verification of Taliban government reports.
cards.body:
Pakistan conducted airstrikes near its border with Afghanistan, killing 13 civilians, according to United Nations confirmation. The Taliban government reported that most of those killed were women and children.

Pakistan said the strikes targeted militant camps operating in Afghan territory. The airstrikes underscore persistent tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban government over militant groups that Pakistan says use Afghan soil to launch attacks across the border into Pakistan.

cards.headline: U.K. Defense Secretary John Healey Resigns Over Military Spending
cards.teaser: British Defense Secretary John Healey resigned, accusing Prime Minister Keir Starmer of failing to invest enough in the military.
cards.body:
John Healey has resigned as U.K. Defense Secretary over disagreements with Prime Minister Keir Starmer regarding military funding. Healey said the government's proposed defence investment plan "falls well short of what is required."

The sudden resignation presents a significant challenge for Starmer's government, raising questions about its defence strategy at a time when European security concerns are mounting and NATO members face pressure to increase military spending.

cards.headline: Netanyahu Aide Charged With Leaking Classified Hamas Negotiations
cards.teaser: Jonatan Urich, a media adviser to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, faces charges of endangering national security over leaked intelligence.
cards.body:
Israeli authorities charged Jonatan Urich, a media adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with passing classified intelligence to a German newspaper. The leaked material concerned negotiations between Israel and Hamas.

Prosecutors accused Urich of endangering Israeli security by disclosing sensitive information about the talks. The case raises questions about information control within Netanyahu's office and the handling of classified material related to Hamas negotiations.

cards.headline: Pope Leo Visits Canary Islands to Highlight Migrant Journeys
cards.teaser: Pope Leo traveled to the Canary Islands to call for humane treatment of migrants seeking better lives.
cards.body:
Pope Leo visited the Canary Islands to spotlight the dangerous journeys undertaken by migrants traveling from West Africa to Europe. During his visit, the Pope called for European nations to treat arriving migrants with compassion and dignity.

The Canary Islands serve as a critical entry point for migrants crossing from West Africa. The Pope's presence underscored the perils these travelers face and urged a humane response to migration rather than rejection.

cards.headline: Global Refugee Numbers Drop Slightly to 118 Million
cards.teaser: The number of forcibly displaced people worldwide fell to nearly 118 million in 2025, though many returned to unstable conditions.
cards.body:
There were nearly 118 million forcibly displaced people worldwide in 2025, a slight decrease from the previous year, according to the United Nations refugee agency. The modest decline marked a rare reduction after years of increases.

Many refugees who returned home went back to countries still facing turmoil, the U.N. said. The agency expressed concern that returning displaced people often face continued insecurity, economic hardship, and lack of basic services in their home countries.

cards.headline: Trump cancels planned strikes on Iran
cards.teaser: The president called off military action scheduled for the evening after discussions about potential negotiations.
cards.body:
President Trump announced the cancellation of planned military strikes against Iran, citing progress toward a peace agreement. Trump claimed the two nations are on the verge of signing a deal and stated that Iranian leadership had approved talks. However, Iranian officials have not yet confirmed these assertions.

The shift represents a dramatic change in approach after recent military exchanges between the US and Iran. Trump has previously made multiple claims about being close to agreements with Iran that were not subsequently confirmed by Iranian leadership.

cards.headline: Pentagon evacuated after false hazardous materials alarm
cards.teaser: The building was partially cleared following a sensor alert that was later determined to be false.
cards.body:
The Pentagon was locked down and partially evacuated after a hazardous materials sensor triggered an alert. Emergency responders arrived at the facility following the alarm. Officials later issued an all-clear after determining the sensor reading was false.

The incident prompted a temporary shelter-in-place order for personnel in affected areas of the building. No actual hazardous materials were found during the emergency response. Normal operations resumed after the all-clear was given.

cards.headline: White House imposes quarantine orders in hantavirus and Ebola responses
cards.teaser: The administration mandated isolation for cruise ship passengers and blocked Americans with Ebola from returning home.
cards.body:
The Trump administration imposed mandatory quarantine orders on two passengers from a cruise ship affected by hantavirus. The administration also blocked Americans who contract Ebola abroad from returning to the United States for treatment.

These measures represent a stricter approach to infectious disease control compared to previous administrations. The policies apply to ongoing outbreaks of both diseases, contrasting with approaches taken during the COVID-19 pandemic.

cards.headline: Study finds poverty affecting brain development in children
cards.teaser: Research on over 2,300 preteens showed socioeconomic factors explained most differences in brain structure.
cards.body:
A study of more than 2,300 children aged nine to ten found that socioeconomic factors accounted for most differences in brain development among preteens. Researchers described the effects as becoming biologically embedded in the brain.

The findings suggest that economic and social circumstances have measurable physical impacts on developing brains during childhood. The study examined brain imaging data to identify structural variations among participants from different socioeconomic backgrounds.

cards.headline: Ebola testing capacity increases in Congo but remains insufficient
cards.teaser: Two facilities now operate near the outbreak's center, but testing may not keep pace with disease spread.
cards.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has expanded its Ebola testing capacity, with two facilities now operating in or near the outbreak's epicenter. This expansion represents progress in the country's response efforts and enables faster diagnosis of suspected cases in affected regions.

However, health officials acknowledge that the current testing infrastructure remains insufficient to keep pace with the rapidly expanding disease. Public health experts have stressed that adequate testing capacity is essential for containing the virus and preventing further transmission.

cards.headline: World Bank Warns Iran Conflict Slowing Global Growth
cards.teaser: The World Bank said the world economy is weakening as energy prices drive a new wave of inflation.
cards.body:
The World Bank issued a warning that ongoing conflict involving Iran is slowing global economic growth. The international financial institution pointed to rising energy prices as a key factor fueling renewed inflationary pressure across multiple economies.

The assessment comes as military tensions in the Middle East have disrupted energy markets and created uncertainty for businesses and governments. Higher energy costs are contributing to broader price increases that threaten to undermine economic expansion in both developed and developing nations. The World Bank's analysis suggests the conflict's economic effects extend well beyond the immediate region.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall After Trump Cancels Iran Strike Plans
cards.teaser: Oil prices dropped after President Trump reversed his threat to launch strikes against Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices declined after President Trump reversed plans to launch military strikes against Iran. The decision came following a second day of escalating military exchanges between the two countries that had raised concerns about wider regional conflict.

Traders had driven prices higher earlier in the day as they anticipated potential disruptions to Middle East oil supplies from an expanded U.S.-Iran confrontation. Trump's cancellation of the strikes eased some market anxiety, though gas prices remain elevated compared to a year ago, with the national average around $4.16 per gallon.

cards.headline: SpaceX Valuation Questioned Ahead of IPO
cards.teaser: Skeptics are raising concerns about whether SpaceX can justify its $1.77 trillion valuation as it prepares for a public offering.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX faces scrutiny over its $1.77 trillion valuation ahead of its planned initial public offering. The company is spending heavily and losing money, prompting questions about whether the valuation can be sustained.

SpaceX has grown rapidly as a leader in commercial space launches and satellite deployment. The company's ambitious spending on technology development and infrastructure has driven significant losses. Investors and analysts are now debating whether the valuation reflects realistic growth prospects or overly optimistic projections. The blockbuster IPO would be one of the largest in history if it proceeds at current valuation levels.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise After Trump Cancels Iran Strikes
cards.teaser: The Dow and Nasdaq moved higher after President Trump called off planned strikes against Iran.
cards.body:
US stock markets rallied after President Trump reversed his decision to launch military strikes against Iran. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 700 points as investors responded to reduced geopolitical risk.

The Nasdaq also posted gains as technology stocks recovered from earlier declines. Markets had fallen during the period of heightened military tensions, with investors concerned about potential disruptions to energy supplies and broader economic stability. The reversal provided relief, though analysts noted that underlying tensions remain unresolved.

cards.headline: Medicare Advantage Plans Frequently Deny Rehab Access
cards.teaser: An analysis found that Medicare Advantage plans often reject requests for short-term nursing home or inpatient rehabilitation services.
cards.body:
Two reports by US investigators revealed that Medicare Advantage plans are quick to deny seniors access to rehabilitation care. The analysis showed that the plans frequently reject requests for short-term nursing home or inpatient services that beneficiaries need.

Medicare Advantage is a private insurance alternative to traditional Medicare, covering more than 30 million seniors. The reports raise concerns about whether the plans are appropriately serving beneficiaries who require post-hospitalization care. Denial rates for rehabilitation services appear significantly higher than in traditional Medicare, potentially forcing seniors to appeal decisions or forgo needed care.

cards.headline: UK Regulators Investigate Ryanair Over Child Seating Fees
cards.teaser: The UK competition regulator is investigating Ryanair over charges the airline imposes on parents to sit next to their children.
cards.body:
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority is investigating Ryanair over charges parents must pay to sit with their children. The airline's terms require at least one parent to accompany children, including those with disabilities, and charges approximately £8 per flight for this seating arrangement.

The regulator noted that Ryanair is the only major carrier operating flights from the UK that imposes such a fee. Ryanair has dismissed the inquiry as "bogus," but the investigation could have implications for how the airline structures its pricing policies going forward.

hero.headline: NASA's Deep Space Network handled Artemis II mission despite strain
hero.body:
NASA's Deep Space Network successfully supported the Artemis II mission despite operating near capacity limits, according to agency officials. The network, which provides communications and tracking for deep space missions, performed well during the crewed lunar flyby that took place in April.

The strain on the network stems from growing demand across multiple missions. Officials noted that some missions are consuming more bandwidth and resources than their initial documentation indicated. This discrepancy has put pressure on the aging infrastructure, which must support an expanding portfolio of lunar, Mars, and deep space exploration programs.

The Deep Space Network consists of three antenna complexes positioned around the globe in California, Spain, and Australia. This arrangement allows continuous communication with spacecraft as Earth rotates. The network has been a backbone of space exploration since the 1960s, but faces increasing demands from both NASA missions and international partners.

The Artemis II mission marked a significant achievement for the space program. The spacecraft carried astronauts around the moon in a test flight for NASA's Space Launch System rocket and Orion crew capsule. Reliable communication throughout the mission was essential for crew safety and mission success.

Looking ahead, NASA faces even greater communication demands. The agency has announced the Artemis III crew, scheduled to launch in 2027. This all-male crew of four includes Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano of the European Space Agency as pilot, along with American astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas. Bresnik serves as mission commander and is a former commander of the International Space Station.

Unlike Artemis II, the Artemis III mission will remain in lower Earth orbit rather than traveling to the moon. The crew will test docking procedures and life support systems for lunar landers from Blue Origin and SpaceX. These tests will prepare for Artemis IV in 2028, which is scheduled to achieve the first crewed lunar landing since 1972.

NASA has been working to upgrade the Deep Space Network to handle these future demands. The agency plans to add new antennas and improve existing equipment to support the Artemis program's long-term goals, including establishing a sustained presence on the Moon and eventual human missions to Mars.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman described the growing constellation of spacecraft needed for upcoming missions as "Earth's first starfleet." Multiple vehicles including Dragon, Soyuz, Starliner, Starship, and Blue Origin landers will eventually operate simultaneously in orbit.

The successful performance during Artemis II, despite the network operating near its limits, demonstrates both the capability of existing infrastructure and the urgent need for planned expansions to support NASA's ambitious exploration agenda.

cards.headline: Meta adds AI assistant and desktop version to Edits video app
cards.teaser: Meta is integrating an AI assistant into Edits and launching a desktop version as it competes with TikTok and YouTube for creator attention.
cards.body:
Meta announced it is adding an AI assistant directly into Edits, its video editing application for creators. The company is also releasing a desktop version of the app, expanding beyond its current mobile-only platform.

The updates aim to keep creators engaged on Instagram as Meta continues its competition with TikTok and YouTube for creator attention and content. The AI assistant is designed to help streamline the video editing process for users producing content for Instagram.

cards.headline: Archaeologists find possible evidence of brain removal in Iron Age Britain
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered scrape marks inside a skull and sharpened long bones that may indicate Iron Age Britons removed brains from the dead.
cards.body:
Archaeologists have discovered scrape marks inside an Iron Age skull from Britain that may indicate deliberate brain removal. The findings suggest the deceased underwent specific post-mortem procedures during this period.

Among other artifacts at the site, researchers identified long bones that appear to have been sharpened into tools. These discoveries together point to intentional mortuary practices involving the treatment of human remains in Iron Age Britain.

cards.headline: Quantum Space pursues $1.2 billion SPAC deal for military spacecraft
cards.teaser: Quantum Space is seeking a $1.2 billion SPAC merger to build military spacecraft, following SpaceX's recent IPO momentum.
cards.body:
Quantum Space announced plans for a $1.2 billion SPAC deal to fund the development of military spacecraft. The company says special purpose acquisition companies remain viable despite recent market skepticism about the investment vehicle.

The timing follows SpaceX's recent initial public offering, which has generated renewed interest in space company investments. Quantum Space aims to capitalize on growing demand for military space capabilities and infrastructure.

cards.headline: Deezer launches tool to detect AI-generated music across streaming platforms
cards.teaser: Deezer introduced a tool that scans playlists from Spotify, Apple Music, and other services to identify music created by artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Deezer has introduced a new tool capable of scanning playlists across multiple streaming services, including Spotify and Apple Music, to identify AI-generated music. The cross-platform functionality allows users to detect artificial content regardless of which service hosts their playlists.

The tool responds to mounting concerns about AI-created music appearing in streaming libraries. As AI technology advances in music production, questions about artist attribution, compensation, and content authenticity have become increasingly pressing for both platforms and listeners.

cards.headline: Multiple countries consider bans on social media for children
cards.teaser: Australia became the first country to ban social media for children in late 2025, with other nations now moving to adopt similar restrictions.
cards.body:
Australia implemented the first national ban on social media for children in late 2025, designed to address cyberbullying, addiction, and predator exposure. The policy marks a significant shift in how governments approach child safety online.

Following Australia's move, other countries are now considering similar restrictions. This emerging trend reflects mounting international concern about social media's effects on young people's development and wellbeing.

cards.headline: Waymo introduces loyalty program with cash back and free cancellations
cards.teaser: Waymo launched a subscription program offering 10% cash back and free cancellations for $29.99 per month.
cards.body:
Waymo has launched Waymo Premier, a monthly subscription program priced at $29.99 that rewards frequent riders with 10% cash back on trips. Subscribers also benefit from penalty-free trip cancellations, making the service more flexible for users.

The loyalty program is designed to build a stable customer base for Waymo's autonomous ride-hailing service. By offering tangible incentives like cash rewards and cancellation flexibility, Waymo aims to encourage regular usage among subscribers committed to the monthly fee.

hero.headline: Real Madrid appoint Mourinho as manager for second time
hero.body:
Real Madrid have announced the appointment of Jose Mourinho as manager for a second spell at the club. The 63-year-old has joined on a three-year contract after leaving Portuguese side Benfica.

Mourinho previously managed Real Madrid from 2010 to 2013, a period that included winning La Liga in the 2011-12 season and the Copa del Rey. He also guided the club to three consecutive Champions League semi-finals during that time, establishing himself as one of Europe's top managers.

The Portuguese coach arrives at the Bernabéu following a turbulent season for the club. Real Madrid's campaign was marked by significant internal difficulties, including player unrest that contributed to the dismissal of previous manager Xabi Alonso in January. Álvaro Arbeloa took over as interim head coach but was unable to reverse the club's fortunes. Real Madrid exited the Champions League at the quarter-final stage to Bayern Munich and finished second in La Liga behind Barcelona. The season was further affected by squad harmony issues, with midfielder Fede Valverde requiring hospital treatment for stitches following a confrontation with teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni.

Mourinho's appointment represents Real Madrid's attempt to restore stability and success to the club. The manager brings extensive experience at the highest level, having won league titles in Portugal, England, Italy, and Spain. His most recent club was Benfica, where he achieved success in European competition. Before joining Benfica last September, Mourinho had managed Roma, where he won the Europa Conference League in 2022.

The announcement also confirms the departure of Arbeloa from his role at the club. The former Real Madrid defender, who played under Mourinho during his first spell at the Bernabéu, took on the interim position following Ancelotti's exit but was ultimately unable to secure the permanent role.

Real Madrid remains one of world football's most successful clubs, holding a record 15 European Cup titles. The club's hierarchy clearly believes Mourinho's proven track record and experience make him the right choice to lead the team back to competing for major honours.

The appointment marks a significant moment in the managerial merry-go-round, with other clubs also reshaping their coaching structures. Marco Silva has agreed to replace Mourinho at Benfica, while Martin O'Neill has been confirmed as Celtic's permanent manager following his success in winning the Scottish Premiership and Cup double.

cards.headline: Broncos sign Sean Payton to five-year contract extension through 2030
cards.teaser: Denver has locked up its head coach with a new deal that runs through the end of the decade.
cards.body:
The Denver Broncos have signed head coach Sean Payton to a five-year contract extension that will keep him through the 2030 season.

Payton arrived in Denver before the 2023 season following his successful stint with the New Orleans Saints, where he won a Super Bowl in 2010 and established himself as one of football's premier offensive strategists.

cards.headline: Falcons acquire offensive tackle Wanya Morris from Chiefs
cards.teaser: Atlanta has made a trade with Kansas City to bolster its offensive line.
cards.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have acquired offensive tackle Wanya Morris from the Kansas City Chiefs, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

Morris was drafted by the Chiefs in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft from the University of Tennessee. The trade bolsters Atlanta's offensive line as the team looks to strengthen its roster.

cards.headline: Brandon Bussi expected to start in goal for Hurricanes in Stanley Cup Final Game 5
cards.teaser: Carolina will turn to its backup goaltender for a critical playoff game.
cards.body: Brandon Bussi is set to be the starting goaltender for the Carolina Hurricanes in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final, marking a change between the pipes for the team as the series progresses.

cards.headline: Jalen Hurts comments on A.J. Brown trade for first time
cards.teaser: The Eagles quarterback addressed the departure of his top receiver.
cards.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts spoke about the A.J. Brown trade for the first time since it became official Wednesday. He briefly reflected on what the pair accomplished during their four years as teammates before turning his attention to the future.

Brown was traded away from Philadelphia in a move that reshapes the Eagles' receiving corps. Hurts and Brown formed one of the most productive quarterback-receiver combinations in the league during their time together in Philadelphia.

cards.headline: Lions taking cautious approach with Brian Branch's recovery from Achilles injury
cards.teaser: Detroit's head coach says the defensive back is progressing but will not rush his return.
cards.body:
Lions head coach Dan Campbell reports that defensive back Brian Branch is progressing well in his recovery from an Achilles tear. The team is taking a measured approach to his return, with Campbell declining to establish a specific timeline for when Branch will be cleared to play.

This cautious strategy underscores the significant nature of Achilles injuries, which typically demand lengthy rehabilitation. The Lions will continue monitoring Branch's progress as the team prepares for the season ahead.

cards.headline: Texas attorney general warns Big 12 against punishing Texas Tech over Brendan Sorsby case
cards.teaser: Ken Paxton sent a letter threatening legal action if the conference takes action against the school.
cards.body:
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sent a letter to Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark and Board of Directors Chairman Douglas Girod regarding Texas Tech's decision to play quarterback Brendan Sorsby. Paxton warned the conference that taking action against the university would expose it to substantial liability.

The letter marks a significant intervention by state officials in conference governance, creating potential legal tension between Texas state government and the Big 12 over the league's authority to discipline member institutions.

hero.headline: Shakira and Burna Boy Open FIFA 2026 World Cup with Performance of Dai Dai
hero.body:
Shakira and Burna Boy performed their collaboration "Dai Dai" at the opening ceremony of the FIFA 2026 World Cup, launching the tournament with a high-energy musical showcase. The performance marked the official start of the competition and introduced the event to a worldwide television audience.

The opening ceremony brought together multiple international acts beyond the headliners. The lineup included appearances from Maná, J Balvin, Los Ángeles Azules, Belinda, and Danny Ocean. This diverse roster of performers reflected the global scope of the tournament and blended different musical genres and traditions on a single stage.

The 2026 World Cup represents a historic moment for the competition. For the first time, the tournament is being hosted across three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The opening ceremony set the tone for the month-long soccer competition that followed. The tournament also expanded to include 48 teams, marking a significant change from the traditional 32-team format used in previous World Cups.

Shakira brings considerable experience to World Cup performances. She has participated in previous tournaments and recorded official World Cup songs, making her involvement in the opening ceremony a continuation of her long association with the event. Burna Boy, a prominent Nigerian artist, brought Afrobeats to the global stage during his collaboration with Shakira, combining his distinctive sound with her pop and Latin influences.

Opening ceremonies have become major cultural events in their own right, extending well beyond the realm of sports. These spectacles blend athletic competition with music and entertainment, creating memorable moments for global audiences. The selection of artists and musical selections typically reflects the host nations while also showcasing the international character of the World Cup.

The performance of "Dai Dai" introduced viewers worldwide to the artistic direction and energy the tournament organizers wanted to convey. By choosing performers from different continents and musical backgrounds, the ceremony emphasized the inclusive and worldwide nature of the competition. The combination of Shakira's established pop and Latin credentials with Burna Boy's rising prominence in Afrobeats created a genuinely international musical moment.

The ceremony's emphasis on musical diversity served practical purposes as well. It appealed to audiences across the three host nations while celebrating the participating countries from around the globe. The choice to feature established artists alongside emerging talent helped bridge different generations of music fans tuning in to watch the tournament's beginning.

As the opening ceremony concluded with the performance of "Dai Dai," it marked the official transition from anticipation to competition. The tournament's expansion to 48 teams and three countries meant that more nations would participate than ever before, and the opening ceremony's musical selections reflected this broader global representation on soccer's biggest stage.

cards.headline: Spider Noir Offers Black and White Viewing Option on Prime Video
cards.teaser: The Prime Video series gives viewers the choice to watch in color or black and white, introducing German expressionist aesthetics to superhero television.
cards.body:
Prime Video's Spider Noir series gives viewers the choice to watch in either color or black and white. This dual-format approach marks a novel direction for superhero television programming.

The black and white aesthetic draws inspiration from German expressionism and employs hard lighting techniques. The creative team incorporated this visual style to introduce comic book audiences to artistic approaches they may not typically see in mainstream superhero productions. Nicolas Cage stars in the series.

cards.headline: Romanian Filmmaker Radu Jude Adapts French Novel Diary of a Chambermaid
cards.teaser: The director released two feature films in 2025 and has already completed a new adaptation in 2026.
cards.body:
Radu Jude has adapted the French classic Diary of a Chambermaid after releasing two feature films in 2025. The Romanian filmmaker competed for both a Golden Bear in Berlin and a Golden Leopard in Locarno with his previous works.

The director continued working in 2026 rather than taking time off between projects. Jude has built a reputation for prolific output and inventive filmmaking approaches across multiple festival circuits.

cards.headline: NBC Submits 11 of 20 Saturday Night Live Hosts for Emmy Consideration
cards.teaser: The network submitted half of Season 51's hosts for guest comedy acting awards, a reduction from previous years.
cards.body:
NBC has submitted 11 out of 20 Saturday Night Live hosts from Season 51 for Emmy consideration in guest comedy acting categories. The Television Academy's ballots reveal which performances the network believes could earn nominations when they are announced on July 8.

The submission list represents a reduction from previous years. Ariana Grande and Connor Storrie are among the hosts being considered, while nine others were not put forward by the network for Emmy voting.

cards.headline: DTF St. Louis Scene Moves From Motel Room to Swimming Pool
cards.teaser: Series creator Steven Conrad and the cinematographer discuss a key scene that transitions from one setting to another.
cards.body:
A pivotal scene in "DTF St. Louis" transitions from a motel room to a swimming pool, encapsulating the show's central themes. Series creator Steven Conrad crafted the sequence to capture both messy psychosexual complications and emotional generosity, moving thematically from sin to caretaking.

The stars, creator, and cinematographer highlighted this scene as key to understanding the series' storytelling approach. The sequence demonstrates how the show balances its complicated themes with character depth and authenticity.

cards.headline: Quiver Distribution Acquires Cyberpunk Thriller Kill Code
cards.teaser: The film stars Frank Grillo, Tyrese Gibson, and Harvey Keitel and will be released on July 24.
cards.body:
Quiver Distribution has acquired domestic rights to Kill Code, a cyberpunk action thriller. The film stars Frank Grillo, Tyrese Gibson, Harvey Keitel, and Franzi Schissler. Justin Price wrote and directed the picture.

The company plans to release Kill Code on July 24. The deal was closed at Cannes, with Voltage Pictures and The Exchange involved in the transaction.

cards.headline: Off Campus Team Denounces Fan Harassment of Cast Members
cards.teaser: The team behind the Amazon Prime Video series warned fans engaging in targeted harassment and threatened to block accounts.
cards.body:
The team behind Amazon Prime Video's Off Campus has denounced fans who engaged in targeted harassment toward cast members and their loved ones. The statement emphasized that the community is built on shared love of storytelling and respect for the people who create it.

The production team threatened to block accounts involved in the harassment. The YA romance series has attracted a dedicated fanbase, but some fan behavior crossed acceptable boundaries according to the show's creators.

hero.headline: Trump cancels planned Iran strikes, cites progress in talks
hero.body:
President Trump canceled planned military strikes against Iran on Thursday, saying discussions with Iranian leadership had reached the highest levels and shown progress. Trump announced the decision in a statement, writing that he had canceled "the forthcoming strikes and bombings" based on developments in talks with Tehran.

The cancellation came hours after Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" following a second night of military exchanges between the two countries. The U.S. military had launched 49 Tomahawk missiles at Iranian targets the previous night. Trump claimed in his announcement that Iran's leadership had "approved" a draft agreement, though Tehran has not confirmed this claim.

Three sources briefed on the negotiations told one news outlet that key gaps in the talks were narrowed during meetings between Iranian officials and Qatari mediators on Wednesday. The discussions reportedly focus on extending a ceasefire, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and beginning 60 days of negotiations on Iran's nuclear program. Qatar has been serving as a mediator between Washington and Tehran.

Trump has previously claimed that a deal with Iran was near, only for negotiations to stall or break down. Iran's top negotiator issued a warning Thursday, saying that "wrong strategies and impulsive decisions will reset the entire board for the worse, explode energy infrastructure and markets and create an endless quagmire." The statement came after Trump had threatened to seize Kharg Island, a central hub for Iran's oil exports.

The situation follows escalating tensions between the two nations, with military strikes exchanged over consecutive nights before the sudden diplomatic shift. The potential agreement under discussion would mark a significant de-escalation if finalized, though details remain subject to confirmation from both governments.

cards.headline: Trump nominates Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence
cards.teaser: The president selected the former SEC chair and current U.S. Attorney to lead the intelligence community.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Thursday that he will nominate Jay Clayton, the current U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, as the permanent Director of National Intelligence. Clayton previously served as chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The nomination comes after widespread criticism of Trump's decision to install Bill Pulte as acting director. Clayton's selection appears aimed at addressing concerns about the leadership of the intelligence community.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats block short-term extension of FISA surveillance powers
cards.teaser: Republicans sought to extend Section 702 spy authority through early July by unanimous consent.
cards.body:
Senate Democrats blocked a Republican attempt Thursday to pass a short-term extension of the nation's foreign surveillance powers. Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas asked the chamber for unanimous consent to extend Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until July 2. Sen. Ron Wyden of Oregon objected to the request, preventing the measure from advancing.

The House also failed to pass a short-term extension of the surveillance law on Thursday, with the measure falling in a 198-218 vote. Democrats announced they would block renewal of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act in protest of Trump's appointment of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance's chief of staff to leave role at end of summer
cards.teaser: Jacob Reses has served as Vance's chief of staff since the vice president took office in January 2025.
cards.body:
Jacob Reses, Vice President Vance's chief of staff, will depart the role at the end of the summer. Reses has worked with Vance since his Senate campaign and continued in the position when Vance took office alongside President Trump in January 2025.

Vance stated that Reses "has been by my side for my whole career in public" service. The announcement did not specify Reses's next plans or who would replace him in the chief of staff position.

cards.headline: Florida Sen. Rick Scott lifts holds on Coast Guard promotions
cards.teaser: The Republican senator had blocked the promotions during a dispute involving a Florida shipbuilder.
cards.body:
Sen. Rick Scott of Florida lifted his holds on Coast Guard promotions, ending a blockade tied to a dispute involving a Florida shipbuilder. Scott had prevented the promotions from advancing through the Senate as part of the disagreement.

The hold affected multiple Coast Guard officers awaiting Senate confirmation for their promotions. Scott's office did not provide details on what resolved the underlying dispute with the shipbuilder.

cards.headline: Republicans file FEC complaint over Alaska Senate candidate with same name as incumbent
cards.teaser: The NRSC asked the commission to investigate Daniel J. Sullivan, who is running as a Republican against Sen. Dan Sullivan.
cards.body:
The National Republican Senatorial Committee filed a complaint Wednesday with the Federal Election Commission regarding an Alaska Senate candidate who shares a name with the state's sitting Republican senator. The complaint targets Daniel J. Sullivan, who is running as a Republican in the same race as incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan.

The NRSC complaint alleges impropriety related to the candidacy of the challenger who shares the senator's name. Alaska law and federal election rules govern how candidates with similar names appear on ballots and conduct campaigns.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio signs sports diplomacy agreement with UFC
cards.teaser: The memorandum establishes a public-private partnership to enhance U.S. sports diplomacy efforts.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and UFC President Dana White signed a memorandum of understanding Thursday creating a new partnership to advance sports diplomacy. The agreement establishes collaboration between the State Department and the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the world's leading mixed martial arts organization.

UFC was founded in the United States and has expanded into a major global sports platform. The State Department characterized the partnership as reflecting U.S. leadership in international sports engagement.
